title_checked: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
decision_reason: The paper equips coding agents with shared forecasting resources, tools, and a self-maintaining workflow and evaluates agent research tasks; it extends the repository record previously cited as ModernTSF.
agent_claim_evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame TSFLab as a workbench that equips compatible coding agents and supports agent-driven research.
claim_summary: TSFLab is an agent-agnostic workbench for time series forecasting research: compatible coding agents share a forecasting research guide, layered knowledge cards for 323 methods, 93 datasets and 71 reusable units, a declarative experiment runner under shared protocols, and a recursive improver that verifies and merges new resources.
evaluation_summary: Paper reproduction (four papers x three attempts) and benchmarking on new data (eight methods x two datasets x three attempts) with Codex CLI against no workbench, TSLib, and TFB, repeated with Claude Code and a second Codex model; module ablations; and a method-development pilot on ETTh1 and Weather. Reported gains: 20-163% higher completion and 11-66% fewer fresh tokens per completed task; the pilot uses 32.8-73.6% fewer fresh tokens and 9.2-68.8% less development time.
corrections: Gains are relative to coding agents without a workbench or with TSLib/TFB under the authors' prompts, budgets, and review criteria.
The method-development pilot covers two datasets and is reported as a pilot study.
notes: Identity and method/evaluation passages checked against the arXiv v1 PDF; not an independent reproduction.

modules.name: Agent-agnostic research workbench
modules.scope_reason: Shared resources and tools are placed outside the agent and exposed to any compatible coding agent without altering it; the mechanism does not depend on temporal semantics or on a task objective.

evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "In contrast, a workbench is plug-and-pla"
evidence.quote: In contrast, a workbench is plug-and-play infrastructure for any compatible agent, such as Claude Code (Anthropic, 2026), Codex (OpenAI, 2026), and Pi (Earendil Works, 2026), benefiting from their continuously improving capabilities.

evidence.locator: PDF p.1; passage beginning "we propose TSFLab, a self-improving agen"
evidence.quote: we propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic “workbench” that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources.

modules.name: Forecasting research guide with task-specific skills
modules.scope_reason: Entry instructions and skills encode forecasting workflows, evaluation settings, and pitfalls such as the forecast target and metric choice, so the guidance is bound to the forecasting task contract.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "TSF-Domain Guide connects this knowledge"
evidence.quote: TSF-Domain Guide connects this knowledge to workbench procedures: entry instructions introduce conventions and module interactions, while 17 task-specific skills provide steps, checks, and pitfalls as needed.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "The skill also requires checking whether"
evidence.quote: The skill also requires checking whether forecasts are evaluated on one target or all variables, keeping metrics consistent across methods.

modules.name: Layered knowledge cards and shared model units
modules.scope_reason: Method and unit cards describe forecasting models, their configurations, and reusable forecasting blocks such as RevIN, so the knowledge structure is organized around forecasting methods.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "It provides a knowledge card for each me"
evidence.quote: It provides a knowledge card for each method, dataset, and unit, organized into summary, card, and source levels.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Knowledge Structurer also extracts commo"
evidence.quote: Knowledge Structurer also extracts common blocks, such as RevIN, series decomposition, and attention variants, into shared units that methods import, enabling shared maintenance; 263 methods reuse at least one unit.

modules.name: Shared temporal data registration and leakage-safe splitting
modules.scope_reason: Dataset cards and shared routines record time fields, sampling frequency, splits, and scaling, and fit scaling on training data only; these temporal data operations are reusable beyond one forecasting method.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Dataset cards record data characteristic"
evidence.quote: Dataset cards record data characteristics and split, scaling, and evaluation protocols.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Shared routines split data as configured"
evidence.quote: Shared routines split data as configured, fit scaling on training data only, select checkpoints on validation data, and compute metrics consistently.

modules.name: Declarative experiment runner under shared protocols
modules.scope_reason: Agents declare experiments with lookback, horizon, and training budget, and results are compared only under the same forecasting protocol, which binds the runner to the forecasting evaluation contract.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "For new-data benchmarking, an agent comb"
evidence.quote: For new-data benchmarking, an agent combines dataset and method presets, fixes the lookback, horizon, and training budget, and sweeps methods and seeds.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Result summaries compare methods only un"
evidence.quote: Result summaries compare methods only under the same data processing, training, and evaluation protocol, reporting seed coverage and variation.

modules.name: Verified self-maintenance of shared resources
modules.scope_reason: Verified outputs and fixes from any session are merged into the shared workbench after usability, complexity, and consistency checks; the improvement mechanism is domain-independent.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Here, self-improvement means incorporati"
evidence.quote: Here, self-improvement means incorporating verified research outputs and fixes into the workbench’s shared resources and workflows so later agents can reuse them.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Recursive Improver brings external resou"
evidence.quote: Recursive Improver brings external resources and agent-produced outcomes back into the shared workbench through checks for usability, complexity, and consistency (Fig. 2d).
